To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“the foamy‐cell liver nodules in Ibarian barbel from Vizela river (Portugal) are a form of macrophage aggregate that may have been induced by water pollution.”

(i) a previously non‐descried liver lesion of Iberian barbels was found; (ii) it was made of macrophages (presumably) and degenerating hepatocyte cells; (iii) it appeared only after a history (at least 3 years) of water quality degradation; and (iv) it was not associated with any parasite.
“foamy‐cells” were found to be a common liver abnormality in the Iberian Barbel from a polluted river in Northern Portugal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first description of this liver lesion type in fish.
the description of the lesion, its etiology and the possible role of macrophage aggregates in liver disease.

the lesion type described herein is a “macroscopic hepatic foamy‐cell nodule” of the Iberia barbel, which could be induced by pollution.
this liver abnormality is a pollution‐related lesion.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liver of the Iberia barbel from the industrialized Vizela River may develop foamy‐cell lesions, which are induced by pollution, and which may be associated with a liver dysfunction.
the liver lesion is not a neoplastic process, but an inflammatory one, induced by pollution, with a probable role in the liver metabolism and/or in the fish immune system.
the lesion was induced by pollution and that it was a form of macrophagic aggregate, which could be considered as a “foamy‐nodule” in the liver of the Iberic barbel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver of the Iberia barbel can present a previously non‐descried lesion type, which can be induced by pollution, and which is worth being included in the list of lesions of the Iberio barbel.

the liver is not only a target organ in fish pollution studies, but it is also an excellent organ to monitor the effects of pollution, because it is the organ with the greatest number of cell types and, consequently, the organ with the highest number of potential lesions.
this liver lesion is not a simple macrophage aggregate, but a more complex lesion that includes degenerating hepatocytes.
